units.title: Counting to 20
units.blurb: Say the numbers in order, count objects one at a time, and know that the last number tells how many.

units.title: Comparing Numbers
units.blurb: Tell which group has more, fewer or the same, and compare written numbers.

units.title: Adding, Taking Away and Teen Numbers
units.blurb: Put groups together, take some away, break numbers into parts, and see teen numbers as ten and some more.

units.title: Measuring and Sorting
units.blurb: Describe and compare things by length and weight, and sort them into groups.

units.title: Shapes
units.blurb: Name shapes in any position, tell flat from solid, and build new shapes.

topics.title: Counting to 10
topics.short: Say the numbers from 1 to 10 in order.
topics.trouble: Children skip or repeat a number name, such as "5, 6, 8," so every count after that is off.

topics.title: Touch and Count
topics.short: Say exactly one number for each object you touch.
topics.trouble: Children touch one object twice or skip one while their counting words keep going.

topics.title: The Last Number Tells How Many
topics.short: The last number you say is how many there are.
topics.trouble: When asked "how many?", children count again from the start instead of repeating the last number they said.

topics.title: Seeing Small Amounts at a Glance
topics.short: Know 1 to 5 dots without counting them one by one.

topics.title: Reading and Writing 0 to 10
topics.short: Match a written number to a group of objects; 0 means none.
topics.trouble: Children do not treat 0 as a number, or write some numerals backward.

topics.title: One More
topics.short: Each counting number is one more than the number before it.

topics.title: Counting Objects to 20
topics.short: Count up to 20 things in a line, a rectangle or a circle.
topics.trouble: When objects are in a circle, children lose track of where they started and count some twice.

topics.title: Counting Out a Number
topics.short: Give exactly the number of objects asked for.
topics.trouble: Children keep counting past the number asked for because they do not stop at the target.

topics.title: Numbers 11 to 20
topics.short: Read and write the teen numbers and 20.
topics.trouble: Children write teen numbers in the order they hear them, so "fourteen" becomes 41.

topics.title: Counting On from Any Number
topics.short: Start counting from a number other than 1.
topics.trouble: Children go back to 1 every time instead of starting from the given number.

topics.title: Counting to 100 by Ones and Tens
topics.short: Count by ones and by tens all the way to 100.
topics.trouble: Children stall where the decade changes, saying "twenty-nine, twenty-ten."

topics.title: More, Fewer or the Same
topics.short: Match or count to compare two groups.
topics.trouble: Children say the group that is more spread out has more, even when it has fewer objects.

topics.title: Comparing Numbers to 10
topics.short: Tell which of two written numbers is greater.

topics.title: Putting Together
topics.short: Adding means joining groups to find how many in all.

topics.title: Taking Away
topics.short: Subtracting means taking some away and counting what is left.
topics.trouble: Children count the objects taken away as the answer instead of the ones left.

topics.title: Writing +, − and =
topics.short: Write a number sentence that matches a story or picture.
topics.trouble: Children think the equals sign means "write the answer now," not "is the same amount as."

topics.title: Story Problems within 10
topics.short: Act out, draw and solve adding and subtracting stories.

topics.title: Breaking Apart Numbers
topics.short: Split a number like 5 into 2 and 3, or 4 and 1.
topics.trouble: Children find only one way to split a number and think it is the only answer.

topics.title: Making 10
topics.short: Find the number that goes with another to make 10.

topics.title: Quick Facts within 5
topics.short: Add and subtract within 5 quickly.

topics.title: Teen Numbers Are Ten and Some More
topics.short: 14 is ten ones and four more ones.
topics.trouble: Children see 14 as a 1 and a 4 side by side, not as ten and four.

topics.title: Long, Tall and Heavy
topics.short: Describe things by length, height or weight.

topics.title: Comparing Lengths and Weights
topics.short: Line things up, or hold them, to see which is longer or heavier.
topics.trouble: Children compare two lengths without lining up the ends, so the one that sticks out looks longer.

topics.title: Sorting and Counting
topics.short: Sort objects into groups, count each group and order them.

topics.title: Position Words
topics.short: Use words like above, below, beside, in front of and behind.

topics.title: Naming Flat Shapes
topics.short: Name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles and hexagons.
topics.trouble: Children say a tilted or upside-down triangle is "not a triangle" because it does not look like the usual picture.

topics.title: Flat and Solid Shapes
topics.short: Tell flat shapes from solid shapes like cubes, cones, cylinders and spheres.
topics.trouble: Children call a cube a square because they name the face they see.

topics.title: Sides and Corners
topics.short: Compare shapes by counting their sides and corners.

topics.title: Building and Combining Shapes
topics.short: Make shapes from parts, and put small shapes together to make bigger ones.
